text:
jordan: Heads up — we're seeing a fast spike in 5xx errors (502/504) for hosted inference after the canary rollout that started ~5m ago. Traffic to /v1/generate is showing timeouts, pages from customers coming in. Can we pause the canary?

oncall-bot: ALERT: svc-gateway: 5xx rate > 8% (5m) — grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/infra?panel=5xx-rate 

maria: I pulled traces — majority show upstream read timeout from the runtime pool. Latency distribution shifted right. Canary config shows the feature flag continuous_batching_enabled=false in canary (should be true). That would disable batching and massively increase per-request GPU load.

jordan: ah that flag flip was part of the release notes but it was supposed to be gated behind model-compat check. Looks like the canary toggled it. Can we revert?

ekelly: Proposed immediate actions: 1) pause further ramp, 2) revert flag for canary, 3) if that doesn't drop errors, rollback canary to previous commit. I'll take 1 and 2.
deploy-bot: Rollout status: release/2026-03-15 -> canary @ 12% traffic. Pause endpoint: rwctl rollout pause --release release/2026-03-15 --env hosted 

luis: Quick repro I ran (from staging agent):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" -H "x-rw-trace: repro-1857" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
* Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
* body: {"error":"upstream read timeout","code":"gateway_timeout"}
```

maria: Stack logs show runtime queue depth spike and repeated KV cache misses — when batching is off latency skyrockets. We're also seeing some 504s from envoy with backend connection reset.

support-bot: CS ticket #10432 (ACME): "API returning 502 intermittently since ~09:12 UTC. Impacting ingestion jobs." Customer is chasing SLA.

ekelly: I'm flipping the flag back on canary now via:
```
# console flag flip (ops-only)
redwood flags set continuous_batching_enabled=true --scope=release/2026-03-15 --env=hosted
```

jordan: While that's happening, pause ramping and notify customers. cs-lead, can you triage ACME and give an ETA?

cs-lead: On it. Notified ACME that we're responding and rolling back risky config — will update in 10m.

maria: After flag flip I expect errors to fall within ~1-2 minutes as prefix caching and batching re-engage. Watch grafana and traces for delta.

deploy-bot: Command executed: rollout paused. Canary remains at 12% traffic.

ekelly: Flag flip confirmed in control plane. Patch pushed to canary configs. Observability: beginning to see regressions down trend.

jordan: Monitoring: 5xx = 7.9% -> 3.1% in last 2 mins, P95 latency down from 1.8s to 420ms. Good sign.

luis: Repro attempt now returns 200, sample trace: x-rw-trace=repro-1857 -> OK.

support-bot: Updated CS ticket #10432: "Mitigated. Engineering reverted a canary config; please verify on your side."

maria: Action items: 1) root cause postmortem: flag gating missing model-compat check (owner: maria), 2) add pre-deploy validation for critical runtime flags (owner: eng-runtime), 3) add automatic canary health stop if 5xx > 5% for 3m (owner: eng-sre).

ekelly: I'll follow up with a rollback of the canary to previous commit if any secondary regressions appear. For now leaving rollout paused until we have +30m of stability.

jordan: Thanks everyone. Quick note: double-check any future flag defaults in release branches. tag @release-managers. :white_check_mark:

maria: I'll start the incident writeup and gather traces/examples for the postmortem.

jordan: Closing thread when we verify 30m stable; leaving open for updates.
